audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Talon 5 of 7 stages while Aurelion Sol wins 54.26% over 258 games; and phases[6].side said 'Skill' against win[6] 'Aurelion Sol'.
audit.why: Level 6 is where Falling Star arrives and Talon has no hard CC to interrupt it, so that row is a genuine coin-flip rather than a Talon stage. The 2+ items row is uncontested for Aurelion Sol and both layers must say so.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = Skill on both layers; 2+ items = Aurelion Sol on both layers. Levels 1-5 stay Talon.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Voice of Light' named as Aurelion Sol's level 6 spike, and 'Rake (W) reset' named as Talon's.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol's R is Falling Star (120/110/100), upgrading to The Skies Descend. Talon's reset is on Noxian Diplomacy (Q, 8/7.5/7/6.5/6), which refunds health and cooldown on a kill — Rake (W, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7) is a returning dagger volley with a slow, no reset. Shadow Assault is 100/80/60.
audit.corrected: Falling Star at 6; Talon's spikes are Q-W-E online by 3 and Shadow Assault at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Talon cannot interrupt Aurelion Sol's channels.
audit.why: Breath of Light (Q) and Astral Flight (W) are interruptible channels, but Riot's text gives Talon no hard CC anywhere in his kit — Rake's returning blades slow, and Assassin's Path and Noxian Diplomacy are movement, not CC. So only his raw damage ends your beam, and Falling Star cannot be cancelled out of your hands. Assassin's Path has a 0s ability cooldown but puts the used terrain on a long cooldown, so a wall he has just vaulted is a wall he cannot re-use immediately.
audit.corrected: Channel through his approach and hold Falling Star for the vault-in; track which wall he has burned.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns is a template and the packet flags zero sequencing advice anywhere on the matchup.
audit.why: Real numbers: Noxian Diplomacy 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Shadow Assault 100/80/60, Astral Flight 22/20.5/19/17.5/16, Falling Star 120/110/100.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the terrain cooldown as the punishable one, plus explicit wait-for-X sequencing.

audit.why: Riot's own description says the returning blades deal bonus damage and slow units hit — no displacement. The flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire and was not written to the page.
audit.corrected: Treated Rake as a slow only.

edits.before: Voice of Light gives you the range to finally zone his approach and start punishing engages
edits.after: Falling Star arrives and nothing in his kit is hard CC, so the stun cannot be taken off you

edits.before: Talon's Rake (W) reset plus Cutthroat (E) leap lets him vault a wall and burst you before you can react, and his early all-in damage far outweighs your slow-projectile trades at this stage.
edits.after: Talon's Assassin's Path (E) vaults any wall on a 0s cooldown and Noxian Diplomacy refunds its own cooldown on a kill, so he arrives from an angle you did not ward and his all-in outweighs your channel trades.

edits.before: Shadow Assault (R) makes him invisible for a devastating burst reset, but this is exactly when Voice of Light comes online for you, giving you range to poke and punish his approach before he closes in.
edits.after: Shadow Assault (R) turns him invisible on a 100s cooldown at rank 1, but this is exactly when Falling Star comes online for you — a stun he cannot interrupt, because nothing in his kit is hard CC.

edits.before: Level 6 is your turning point — Voice of Light gives you the range to poke and zone him before he can close the gap, forcing him to work harder for his engage. Respect his Shadow Assault invisibility for repositioning plays, but you can now punish his approach with damage of your own instead of just surviving it.
edits.after: Level 6 is your turning point — Falling Star is a stun he cannot interrupt, since Rake only slows and nothing else in his kit is hard CC. Hold it for the moment he vaults in rather than spending it on the wave. Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1, so a spent ultimate leaves a long window where he has to walk at you.

edits.before: After level 6, poke aggressively with R to zone his approach before he can flank
edits.after: After level 6, save Falling Star as the stun for his vault-in, not for poke

edits.before: Vault a wall with Cutthroat (E) to close distance instantly and burst with Rake resets
edits.after: Vault a wall with Assassin's Path (E) to close instantly and burst you from melee

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. It governs your forward steps. - W Astral Flight spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Assassin's Path costs nothing, but the wall he just vaulted goes on a long cooldown — step up on that side. - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and the return blades carry the slow; stand off the return line. - Wait for Shadow Assault to be spent before you commit Astral Flight.

edits.before: The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Stand where Rake's return blades miss — the second pass is the damage. Freeze until Falling Star is up, then he has to walk in.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Talon for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: He has no CC to cancel Falling Star, so the only way you lose it is by dying first — keep Flash for the vault and the stun for the landing.

edits.before: Your flight is your only escape — a W spent poking is a death sentence against the next gank.
edits.after: Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1 and it is your only exit from a wall vault you did not see coming.

edits.before: If Talon takes first blood, tighten up: Rake is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with E executes and stay relevant through the stardust curve.
edits.after: If Talon takes first blood, ward the walls behind you, not the river — his entry is terrain, not the lane. A second kill ends the duel, not the game: clear with E executes and keep banking stardust.

notes: Two fabricated names removed: 'Cutthroat (E)' (Talon's E is Assassin's Path) and 'Voice of Light' (Aurelion Sol's R is Falling Star / The Skies Descend). 'Rake reset' was also wrong — the refund is on Noxian Diplomacy (Q). Rake's derived 'knockup' flag contradicts Riot's description, which says slow only; the description was trusted. Level chart: phases[6].side/win[6] disagreed and was fixed; Level 6 was additionally flipped to Skill on both layers to address the packet defect 'level chart contradicts data' — Aurelion Sol wins 54.26% while the chart gave Talon 5 of 7 stages, and Falling Star landing uninterruptible against a kit with no hard CC is the reason that row is not his.
